b0.script: [coaxing, confident, smiling] Come on, honey. Deedee has not missed a dance floor in fifty years. [counting in, brisk] One, two, three.

b1.script: [cheerful hostess, firm, then joyful] Shoes off, everybody! Floors just mopped! Let us DANCE!

b2.script: [bright, warm, upbeat] Room for one more? Deedee brings cookies, hugs, and love to the moon and back!

b4.script: [loving, clear, beaming] Girls! I love you to the moon and back!

b5.script: [cheerful offer] Who wants rhubarb crisp? [matter-of-fact, firm] Everyone wants rhubarb crisp.

b6.script: [brisk, fond, in charge] Hold still! You've got a smudge!

b7.script: [brisk, then satisfied] Spit shine! There. Much better.

b8.script: [energetic power-walker, upbeat] Ten thousand steps! Keep up, honey!

b9.script: [brisk nurse, kind, confident] Retired registered nurse! Little pinch, honey!

b10.script: [firm, house-proud, not angry] I just mopped! Watch your step!

b11.script: [proud, warning, warm] Fresh rhubarb crisp! Careful, it's HOT!

b12.script: [cheeky, bright laugh] Just one glass! It's five o'clock somewhere!

b13.script: [calling across the house, strong, warm] Dinner's ready! Nobody leaves this table hungry!

b14.script: [building, loving, then shouting with joy] I love you to the moon... AND BACK!

b15.script: [brisk, playful, in charge] Dish-towel flick. You had a spot.

b16.script: [cheerful nurse, confident] Registered nut, reporting. [caring, firm] Let me see that.

b17.script: [warm, conspiratorial] Corner-piece privilege. I saved the good bit.

b18.script: [firm, final, calm authority] Oven mitt ultimatum. Enough of that.

b19.script: [energetic coach, brisk] Brisk means brisk. Keep your arms moving.

b20.script: [gentle, teasing, kind] Garden shower. You looked a little wilted.

b21.script: [bright, energetic morning voice] Rise and shine! The day is wasting!

b23.script: [Long Island accent, energetic grandma, proud and grand, announcing like a superhero] I am the Beanie Master!

b24.script: [loving, arms wide, strong] Come here, you! One big squeeze!

b25.script: [calling across the house, firm and warm] Wash your hands, everybody! Sunday dinner is on the table!

b26.script: [building, then shouting with joy] Hold on tight! I love this family to the moon and back!

b27.script: [scandalized, delighted gossip] Did you SEE what it was wearing?

b28.script: [brisk, encouraging, in charge] Faster, honey! Clean as you go!

b29.script: [proud, organized, delighted with herself] Rome, then Florence, then the coast. I made a binder.

b30.script: [hostess, firm, fond, quick] Everybody eat! [correcting] Wait, the gumbo goes HERE. [firm] Elbows off!

b31.script: [gardener, encouraging shout] Pull, honey! Roots and all!

b32.script: [tasting, then sharp, house-proud] Needs salt. [firm] Who cleaned this counter?!

b33.script: [tender, sincere, strong] Fifty-one years, Boppy. [warm, sure] I'd do every single day again!

b34.script: [warm, arms wide, bright] To the moon and back! Everybody in!

b35.script: [loving, insistent, laughing] Group hug! Tommy, you too!

b36.script: [shocked, indignant, dignified] Oh! Well, I never!

b37.script: [pained, then nurse matter-of-fact] Ow! That needs ice. Trust me, I'm a nurse!

b38.script: [catching her breath, composed, kind] Deedee needs a little sit-down, girls.

b39.script: [composed, dry, a little funny] Somebody pour me a glass of wine.

b40.script: [calm, insisting, half joking] I'm just resting my eyes.

b41.script: [cheering, generous, bright] Rhubarb crisp for everyone! You earned it!

b42.script: [proud, beaming] My girls did it! To the moon and back!

b43.script: [energetic coach, brisk, fond] Keep up, honey! Arms at ninety!

d44.script: [pleased, proud of both of them] Your bread and my rhubarb crisp. Now THAT is a meal.

d45.script: [spotting a clue, sharp and bright] Crumbs! Rhubarb crumbs. [on the hunt] That little thief went right through here.

d46.script: [nurse, brisk and loving] Up, up. Everybody up. [tender] Deedee kisses it better.

d47.script: [satisfied, then firm with a smile] There. Good as new. Try not to do that again.

d48.script: [warm, strong hug] Hugs for everyone. [satisfied] There. All better.

d49.script: [calm commander, clear, confident] Tommy, you stand in front of whoever it stares at. Rosie, make it laugh. Then we try again.

d50.script: [relieved, delighted] My tin! And look. Half the crisp is still in it.

d51.script: [decisive, warm] Then we split this half. Everybody home. [eager] Boppy has to hear about this.

d52.script: [hostess, firm, cheerful] Sit. Everybody sit. Half a crisp is still a crisp.

d53.script: [brisk, cheerful, running the house] Rhubarb crisp in the oven, dinner on the stove, floors just mopped. [firm] Shoes off. [bright] Who wants a cookie?

d54.script: [loving, then playfully firm] Grace, Rose, Deedee loves you to the moon and back. Say it back. [coaxing] Louder.

d55.script: [nurse mother, sharp-eyed, firm] Tommy, is that a bruise? Sit. Eat. Explain.

d56.script: [cheerful, matter-of-fact, a little proud] I baked at five this morning. The neighbors have stopped asking why.

d57.script: [loving, emphatic, making sure they hear it] To the moon and back, girls. The MOON. And BACK.

d58.script: [inviting, bright] Grace, Rose, who wants to help Deedee frost something?

d59.script: [brisk, proud, then dry] I already did my walk. Boppy did one lap around the recliner.

d60.script: [firm, house-proud, not angry] I just cleaned the floors. Shoes OFF.

d61.script: [matter-of-fact, then pointed and funny] Retired registered nurse. Tom calls me a registered nut. [threat with a smile] Tom is due for a checkup.

d62.script: [firm, clear, house rule] Sunday dinner is at five. Five means four thirty.

d63.script: [warm, strong hug] Hugs for everyone, just because. To the moon and back.

d64.script: [fussing, worried] Are you warm enough? [certain] Nobody is warm enough.

d65.script: [cheerleader, sing-song] Grace, Rose, to the moon and back. Say it. [shouting happily] LOUDER.

d66.script: [brisk power walker] Pick up those feet. [cheerful] A brisk walk never hurt anybody.

d67.script: [concerned nurse, peering at him] Tommy, you look pale. When did you last drink water? [firm] Nurse is asking.

d68.script: [tender, strong, to the whole table] To the moon and BACK.

d69.script: [warm, a little sad, waving him off] Oh, Tommy. Somebody has to stay with my angels. [practical] And the pies.

d70.script: [pressing a bag into his hands] Here. Cookies for the flight. [tender] To the moon and back, honey.

d76.script: [warm, brisk, wry] Not today, honey. Book club at four. [dry] We are reading the same book as last month. [wry] Nobody finished it.

d77.script: [energetic grandma, distracted, sweet] Not yet, honey. I am still deciding on earrings. [bright] Come back with the invitation.

d78.script: [energetic grandma, brisk, fast] Not this time, honey. Somebody has to start Sunday dinner. [dry] Every clock in my kitchen says midnight and the roast does not care.

d79.script: [beaming, gathering them in] And my girls! Come here, come here.

d84.script: [warm praise, then brisk] Good job, girls. The crumbs keep going north.

d97.script: [delighted, arms open, gathering them in] There's my Tommy! And my girls! Come here, come here.

d104.script: [fond, firm, taking charge] Tom, you are skin and bones. Sit. [brisk] The crisp needs ten minutes on the counter.

d105.script: [outraged about the tin, then decisive] That is my GOOD tin! [brisk, no argument] Grab your shoes. I am coming with you.

d106.script: [quick nurse check, then firm] Everybody okay? Itchy is not hurt. Keep walking.

d107.script: [tracking, matter-of-fact, a knowing note on Boppy] The crumbs go around the pond. Toward Boppy's fishing spot.

d108.script: [indignant, fierce, a little funny] That is my GOOD tin, you overgrown handbag!

d109.script: [delighted, looking him over] Back already! Look at you. Did they feed you out there? [decided] Never mind. I will feed you.

d110.script: [practical, then firm nurse order] I have three pies in, so I am staying put. [pointed] Do NOT let him eat peppers on an empty stomach.

d111.script: [calm, final, not up for discussion] You are wearing the tie.

d112.script: [remembering, wistful but clear] Forty years I have lived in this town. Every full moon, the lights used to go on in that dome above Luna's. [quiet] Nobody I know has ever been invited. Not once.

d113.script: [hushed, moved] Oh. Oh, Tommy. It is beautiful.

d114.script: [snapping back to practical, appalled, brisk] It is FILTHY. Fifty years of dust. Somebody hand me a mop.

d115.script: [recognizing it, hushed, certain] Purple velvet. Tommy. That is Aunt Ellie's coat.

d116.script: [warm, knowing, fond of Ellie] We will tell her, honey. She will be so pleased. [smiling] She will pretend not to be. That is how you know.

d117.script: [awed, urgent] Tommy. Over the bandstand. It is so BRIGHT. [laughing at herself] I cannot look at it. I am looking at it.

d118.script: [reasonable, firm, a touch of humor] Honey, there is a whole town walking into hedges down there.

d119.script: [kind, reassuring, warm promise] Oh, honey. Nobody has to turn off the lights. We will come back. Every full moon. [smiling] I will bring crisp.

d120.script: [thinking it through, practical, dry] Somebody invited you up here, Tommy. Not her. She cannot hold a pen. [plain] She is a ball.

d121.script: [soft, realizing, touched] Somebody who knew you would come. And that you would bring your mother.

d122.script: [surprised, a little flustered, laughing at herself] Tommy, there was something else in the envelope. Stuck to the bottom. I did not see it. I read it eleven times and I did not see it.

d123.script: [overjoyed, emotional, then brisk and funny] THERE they are. Tommy! The oven clock started blinking twelve oh one and I cried a little. [matter-of-fact] Into the gravy. It is fine. It is seasoning.

d124.script: [hostess running the table, firm, fast, fond] Everybody sit. Everybody. Justin, you too. Ellie, that is Boppy's chair. Boppy, that is my chair. [warning tone, loving] Boppy.

d129.script: [firm with her husband, kind, practical nurse] He is a guest, Boppy. Sit. He can sit next to you. [dry] You could use the cold on that knee.

d130.script: [proud gardener, no argument] The tomatoes are coming in. You are going home with forty.

d131.script: [dry, fond, a wife's report] Boppy says he is not feeling good. Boppy also will not stop fishing.

d132.script: [cheeky, warm] A little glass of wine with dinner. Just one. [official] Nurse's orders.

d133.script: [firm, then giving in with a smile] Rhubarb crisp is cooling on the counter. Do not touch it. [relenting] Okay, one corner.

d134.script: [cheerful, then realizing, then decisive] I packed cookies. They are in my purse. [beat] The purse is at home. [brisk] We go back.

d135.script: [firm, loving] When we get home I am making a big dinner. [no arguments] Nobody argue.

d137.script: [bright welcome, curious] There they are! Well? Did anybody catch anything?

d139.script: [flat, knowing, one eyebrow up] Did he.

d140.script: [fond, firm, in charge of the table] Sit down, you. I made rhubarb crisp. Everybody sit. [pointed, to Boppy] And eat SLOWLY.

d141.script: [tender, then brisk] I love you all to the moon and back. Now eat.

d142.script: [warm, firm] Not this time, honey. I have three pies in and Boppy needs somebody to go fishing with. [bright] Take the girls.

d143.script: [warm, firm, brisk] Not tonight, honey. I made a plate for the teachers. [wry] Somebody has to keep Boppy away from it.

d144.script: [excited, flustered, bright] Tommy! There you are. Sit. No, stand. Read it. Read it out loud. [breathless] I have read it eleven times.

d145.script: [concerned, then indignant and a little funny] And now the moon is missing. Three nights. I power walk at nine. I walked straight into the Hendersons' hedge.

d146.script: [gentle prompt, warm] Honey, show her the seal.

d147.script: [reading aloud, curious, then sharp] The plaque says MEMBERS ARE ADMITTED BY MOONLIGHT. And look, three little brass stands. [noticing] Somebody took the mirrors.

d148.script: [calm nurse, brisk and kind] Okay, everybody up. Deedee is a nurse. Up, up. Little sip of water. [approving] Good.

d149.script: [affectionate teasing, settled fact] You ARE a sore loser, honey.

d150.script: [proud, teasing her husband] Look at you. Making a friend.

d151.script: [kind, gentle, understanding] Oh, sweetheart. Nobody asked you to dance, did they?

d152.script: [touched, smiling, to the room] Fifty-two years, and he still asks. Every time.

d153.script: [thrilled, giddy] Admitted by moonlight. Oh, I have goosebumps. Tommy, feel my arm.

d154.script: [brisk nurse, calm] Up, everybody. Deedee is a nurse.

d155.script: [amused, unbothered, still firm] Then sway with your mother.

d156.script: [firm, loving, not a request] Tommy. Dance with your mother.

d157.script: [bursting to tell her, bright, warm] Ellie. There was a BALL. A big silver one. She remembered you. [proud] And look what we brought home.

d158.script: [thrilled, counting it out] Admit three, Tommy. You. Me. [decided] And Boppy.

d159.script: [dry, loving, correcting her husband] You drove into the mailbox twice, honey.

d160.script: [clear coach, then softer and knowing] Tommy, whatever her shiny side shows bounces right back. Use something else. [gentle] And honey, nobody has asked her to dance since nineteen seventy one. Three times.

d71.script: [gasping, scandalized, delighted] On her BIRTHDAY. [calling over her shoulder] Boppy, did you hear that?

d72.script: [patting her pockets, flustered, laughing at herself] I had them. [insisting] I had them a MINUTE ago.

d73.script: [warm, holding up a hand] Hold on, honey. Let me read the cake box first. [careful, serious] It has to say dairy free. [patting her pockets, muttering] Where are my glasses.

d74.script: [loving, strong] To the moon and back, Rosie. [bigger] The MOON. [joyful, emphatic] And BACK.

d75.script: [proud, reassuring] Cake is on the counter. Dairy free. [laughing at herself] I read the box nine times. [triumphant] With my glasses.

d80.script: [bright, flustered, searching] Where are my reading glasses? I had them one second ago. [hurried] I need to read the timer.

d81.script: [noticing, amused, a little sheepish] So they are. [conspiratorial whisper] Not one word to Boppy.

d82.script: [cheerful, holding up two fingers] A sliver for me. Just a sliver. [matter-of-fact, unbothered] Sourdough gives me gas.

d83.script: [warm, loving, a little smug] And I eat it anyway. [tender] That's love, Tommy.

d85.script: [brisk, waving it off] Not one pepper for me either. [matter-of-fact] Peppers give me gas.

d86.script: [flat, narrowing her eyes, amused] Who told you that.

d87.script: [mock-stern, teasing, smiling] Tata is on thin ice.

d88.script: [eager, holding out her hand] Hand me my glasses. I want to look at him properly. [exasperated, laughing] Where ARE my glasses.

d89.script: [warm, grateful] Thank you, Rosie. [settling in, fond] Now. Let me look at him.

d90.script: [bright, squinting, cheerful] Somebody read me that plaque. [laughing at herself] My glasses are in my other purse.

d91.script: [surprised, then dignified and amused] Oh. So I am. [brisk] Well then.

d92.script: [defensive, laughing, a little indignant] I couldn't FIND them, honey.

d93.script: [polite but firm, smiling] None for me, Justin. [matter-of-fact] Store-bought gives me gas.

d94.script: [giving in, warm, touched] Fine. One slice. [tender] For the girl who said it.

d95.script: [calling out, bright, flustered] And has anybody seen my glasses? [laughing] I can't read the oven.

d96.script: [knowing, dry, fond] Of course they are. [firm, house rule] Nobody touch the butter.

d98.script: [bright, searching, flustered] Have you seen my reading glasses? I had them a minute ago. [exasperated, laughing] I've looked everywhere. [emphatic] Twice.

d99.script: [triumphant, then sheepish] Found my glasses. [beat] They were in the fridge. [quick, firm] Don't ask. [bright, cheerful] Who wants a cookie?

d100.script: [good-natured, waving them off] All right, all right. The pies need me anyway. [warm, inviting] Come back for a cookie.

d101.script: [cheerful, hands on hips, playfully firm] Now hold on, Tommy. You're not taking my angels anywhere without me and a bag of cookies. [hopeful, sweet] Can Deedee come along?

d102.script: [delighted, clapping] Wonderful! Everybody hold hands. [fond, insisting] Tommy, you too. [joyful, rallying] To the moon and back, here we come.

d103.script: [warm, practical] Oh, honey. Somebody has to stay and mind the house. [curious, brisk] Who's it going to be?

d125.script: [delighted, arms open] There's my Tommy! And my girls! [slowing, confused] And my... [alarmed] oh. OH. [baffled, nurse taking charge] Why is Rose in an ice cube.

d126.script: [sheepish, amused, quiet] ...So they are. [firm whisper] Don't say anything.

d127.script: [reading carefully, satisfied] Dairy free. Good. [shifting into nurse mode, tender] Now. Rose. Come here, sweetheart. [warm, sure] Deedee's got you.

d128.script: [calm, confident nurse, kind] Cold doesn't beat cold, Tommy. Warm beats cold. [firm, smiling] Always has. [wry] Ask any nurse.

d161.script: [bright, bustling, delighted] Tommy! Sit. Eat. I made a crisp. [laughing, unapologetic] It is nine in the morning and it is a crisp. [playfully firm] Do not argue.

d162.script: [excited, then fussing over him warmly] A layover! Where? [waving it off] Never mind. Take a sweater. [quicker] Take two. [pressing it into his hands] Take the crisp.

d163.script: [tender, loving, strong] To the moon and back, Tommy. [soft, sure] Both ways.
